document: OC Closure Setup (new Angular page) and stock write-off configuration
title: What happens to the stock when an OC is closed?
content: When an OC is closed the system automatically returns and transfers out of system the material or OC stock of that closed OC. With the write-off configuration, the leftover stock is transferred to the write-off site instead.
where_used: Admin > Configurator > Configuration Rules > OC Closure Setup
notes: The backend must enable the new consumption marking. Once the OC Closure Setup is done you do not need the miscellaneous setting Enable Write off for Site.

document: OC Closure Setup (new Angular page) and stock write-off configuration
title: What must be done before using the OC Closure Setup?
content: Create a write-off site in the site master (mark the site as a write-off site) so that material can be transferred to the write-off site directly. Then open the new submenu OC Closure Setup under Admin > Configurator > Configuration Rules.
steps:
1. Ask the backend team to enable the new consumption marking.
2. In the site master create the write-off site (Is write off site).
3. Open Admin > Configurator > Configuration Rules > OC Closure Setup.
4. Select company, site, write-off site, category, stock rule, transaction type and execution type.

document: OC Closure Setup (new Angular page) and stock write-off configuration
title: How do I configure the OC Closure Setup?
content: Open Admin > Configurator > Configuration Rules > OC Closure Setup and add a row per company: choose the inventory site, the write-off site, the category, the stock rule, the transaction type (for example FPPO) and the execution type (Factory or Outsourced), then the WIP rule, and switch the Enable toggle on. After this, when an OC is closed the leftover stock goes to the write-off site or out of system, as the rule says.
steps:
1. Have the backend team enable the new consumption marking.
2. Create the write-off site in the site master.
3. Open Admin > Configurator > Configuration Rules > OC Closure Setup and click Add.
4. Select the member company, inventory site, write-off site and category.
5. Select the stock rule (OC Stock write off + Un-Reserve, or OC Stock Transfer out of system).
6. Select the transaction type and the execution type; add more categories, transaction types or execution types with the Add buttons if needed.
7. Select the WIP rule if needed, and for write-off the cost centre and inventory reason.
8. Switch on the Enable toggle.
where_used: Admin > Configurator > Configuration Rules > OC Closure Setup
notes: One WIP site is mandatory in the member company and duplicate rows are not allowed.

document: OC Closure Setup (new Angular page) and stock write-off configuration
title: How do I create or choose the write-off site?
content: Create the write-off site in the site master and mark it with the option Is write off site. In the OC Closure Setup the Write Off Site list then shows only those sites, for the selected member company, and you pick the write-off site there.
where_used: Site master; Admin > Configurator > Configuration Rules > OC Closure Setup

document: OC Closure Setup (new Angular page) and stock write-off configuration
title: What fields are on the OC Closure Setup screen?
content: Member Company, Inventory Site, Write Off Site, Category, Stock Rule, Transaction Type, Execution Type, Enable toggle, WIP Rule, Inventory Reason (TOS), CM Company Rule toggle, Cost Center and Inventory Reason (CM Transfer to Site). Toolbar: Add, Add Category, Add Transaction Type, Add Execution Type, Delete and Activity Timeline.
notes: Member Company is a single-selection list. Inventory Site comes from the Site Master for the selected member company. Write Off Site lists only sites marked Is write off site, for the selected member company. Category comes from the Category master. Transaction Type is single-selection (for example FPPO). Execution Type is Factory (own factory and other factory) or Outsourced. The Activity Timeline shows an Activity Log (changes captured) and a Change Log (history of changes).

document: OC Closure Setup (new Angular page) and stock write-off configuration
title: What are the stock rules of the OC Closure Setup?
content: There are two stock rules. OC Stock write off + Un-Reserve: after OC closure the OC stock is first transferred to the write-off site and the stock is unreserved from that site. OC Stock Transfer out of system: after OC closure the stock of the closed OC is transferred out of system automatically.
notes: If a stock rule is selected, the WIP rule is not mandatory. If OC stock write off + Un-Reserve is selected, the CM Company Rule is frozen and Write Off Site, Cost Centre and Inventory Reason (CM Transfer To Site) become mandatory.

document: OC Closure Setup (new Angular page) and stock write-off configuration
title: What are the WIP rules of the OC Closure Setup?
content: Issued Return + Transfer Out of system: the material first returns to the site, then is transferred out of system. Issued Return: the material returns to the site. Issued Return + write off: the material first returns to the site, then is transferred to the write-off site.
notes: Example: 100 MTR was issued to the floor and 90 MTR consumed; when the OC is closed 10 MTR returns to the site and is transferred out of system. A blank option is provided so a user who picked the WIP rule by mistake can clear it.

document: OC Closure Setup (new Angular page) and stock write-off configuration
title: How does the CM Company Rule work when the OC is in one company and production in another?
content: When the CM Company Rule toggle is on, the rule is applied to the CM company. Example: the OC is created in Company A and production happens in Company B. When the user closes the OC from Company A, the material returns from the production floor site to the Company B site, and the system creates an automatic GDI, GDN and GRN in Company B (receipt type Transfer to site). It then returns from the Company B site to the Company A site with an automatic GDI, GDN and GRN (receipt type Transfer to site). In Company A the action of the selected WIP or stock rule is taken.
notes: The CM reason can only be entered when the CM toggle is on.

document: OC Closure Setup (new Angular page) and stock write-off configuration
topic: OC closure reasons and cost centre
title: Where do the inventory reason and cost centre of OC closure come from?
content: Inventory Reason (TOS) and Inventory Reason (CM Transfer to Site) come from the Reason for Correction master (Inventory > Codes > Reason for Corrections), showing only reasons whose transaction type is Transfer Out of System or All. Cost Center comes from the Cost Center master (FA > Master definition > General Master > Cost Center category).

document: OC Closure Setup (new Angular page) and stock write-off configuration
title: What validations does the OC Closure Setup have?
content: One WIP site must be selected for the member company, and duplicate rows are not allowed. Version 1.0 of the specification was created by Sumit Sharma on 28 January 2025.

document: Sample Order Manual (Classic Fashion)
title: How does the sample order process work?
content: The sample order covers creating a sample order, the sample BOM, the sample supplier PO, and sample receipt and dispatch. The flow is: new sample order, confirm, create the BOM, view and release requirements (indents), receive the sample, then dispatch it by courier or forwarder.
where_used: Sales > Sample Order > New Sample Order

document: Sample Order Manual (Classic Fashion)
title: What are the copy options of a sample order?
content: Copy and create new style: copies the style information and creates a new techpack after confirmation. Copy and create variant: same, and keeps a link between the parent style and the copied styles. Copy Style: copies the style information without creating a new techpack. Copy sample order: copies the sample information without creating a new techpack.

document: Sample Order Manual (Classic Fashion)
title: What fields are filled on a new sample order?
content: Sample Order No. (system generated), Created On, Article Code, Buyer, Buyer Department, Season, Supplier Name, Buyer Contact, Supplier Contact, Worksheet Received On, Buyer Delivery Date. Style details: Material Type, Fabric/Main Material, Product Group/Sub Category, Gender, Article Description, Buyer Target Price, Buyer Quoted Price, Supplier Quoted Price, UOM, Internal Reference, Wash Type, Product Finishing, Iron Type, Embroidery Type, Print Type and Master Style.

document: Sample Order Manual (Classic Fashion)
title: How do I add the sizes of a sample order?
content: Under Sample Order Details first select the required sizes, then click Add. The related details appear to be filled; fields in red are mandatory. Click Confirm at the top of the page. The details then appear on the Sample Order View screen, where the Bill of Material is created.

document: Sample Order Manual (Classic Fashion)
title: How do I create the BOM of a sample order?
content: From the Sample Order View open Bill of Material and choose one of three options: create a new BOM using a layout, copy from an article (another article sampling BOM), or copy from this article’s production Bill of Material (when the sample style is copied from an existing style). The categories shown (for example Fabric and Trims) depend on the layout chosen.
steps:
1. Choose the BOM option and click OK.
2. Click Add and fill article, body type, colour, size, UOM, consumption quantity, wastage, product quantity and the other details.
3. Click View Requirement and check the details.
4. Click Release Requirements so that indents are generated.
5. Find the indents in Sourcing > Indent Management > User Indent List and fulfil them.
where_used: Sourcing > Indent Management > User Indent List
notes: For indent fulfilment and receiving material see the Indent Management and Inventory manual.

document: Sample Order Manual (Classic Fashion)
title: How do I receive a sample from the sample room?
content: When the sample is ready in the sample room it is received with a Sample Receipt before it is dispatched to the buyer.
steps:
1. Open Sales > Sample Order > Sample Receipt.
2. Fill the supplier, the supplier document reference number and the site where you want to receive the sample.
3. Click Add and select the sample orders (several can be selected).
4. Click Confirm.
5. Find the receipt in Sales > Sample Order > Sample Receipt List.

document: Sample Order Manual (Classic Fashion)
title: How do I dispatch a sample to the buyer?
content: There are two dispatch options: Sample Courier Dispatch (through a courier) and Sample Forwarder Dispatch (through a forwarder). Fill the details, select the order and Confirm.
where_used: Sales > Sample Order > Sample Courier Dispatch or Sample Forwarder Dispatch
notes: The dispatch orders can be seen in Sales > Sample Order > Sample Dispatch List.

document: Sample Order Manual (Classic Fashion)
title: How do I receive a sample that the buyer sends back?
content: The sample must have been dispatched as Returnable. Then do one more transaction, the Buyer Returned Sample Receipt. It then appears in the Buyer Returned Sample Receipt List.
steps:
1. Dispatch the sample with Type = Returnable (a Non-Returnable sample cannot be received back).
2. Open Sales > Sample Order > Buyer Returned Sample Receipt and create the receipt.
3. Find it in Sales > Sample Order > Buyer Returned Sample Receipt List.
where_used: Sales > Sample Order > Buyer Returned Sample Receipt

document: Sample Order Manual (Classic Fashion)
title: What is the difference between returnable and non-returnable samples?
content: On the dispatch screen the Type is Returnable or Non-Returnable. With Non-Returnable you cannot receive any sample the buyer sends back. With Returnable you can, with one more transaction: the Buyer Returned Sample Receipt.
where_used: Sales > Sample Order > Buyer Returned Sample Receipt (list: Buyer Returned Sample Receipt List)

document: Sample Order Manual (Classic Fashion)
title: How do I create an invoice for courier dispatches?
content: Create a Courier Invoice. It can consolidate several dispatches into one courier invoice: select the dispatches, click OK and confirm.
